newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says he trusts judicial system.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says he trusts judicial system.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi reacted calmly on Monday to reports that a magistrate had asked for him to be put on trial, saying he had faith in the Italian judicial system.

"I trust in justice," Prodi told reporters in northeast Italy. It was his first response to news agency reports that a Rome magistrate had asked for him to be charged with abuse of office over dealings when he was chairman of state holding IRI.

The AGI and ANSA news agencies earlier said the request by the magistrate, Giuseppa Geremia, related to the sale by IRI in 1993 of the food unit Cirio to Fis.Vi, a consortium of agricultural cooperatives.
The reports said the request for the indictment of Prodi and five other members of the 1993 IRI board would be considered by an examining judge.
"The indictment request certainly does not put my personal honesty at stake," Prodi told a news conference in the northeast town of Udine, where he was on a visit.

"The offence concerned is one which the entire board of IRI has been called to account over...I shall clarify everything as I have always done. I have always had complete trust in justice and this is not a problem."
